DELIVERED: the manifest compiles to four targets (CSS custom properties with an @supports OKLCh upgrade, TypeScript constants, React Native styles, a Tailwind v4 theme), every output committed and BYTE-COMPARED by its tests; gate 9 (contrast) ACTIVE and BLOCKING after being watched fail on five real defects, with an eight-case mutation proof in CI (scripts/verify-contrast-proof.mjs) asserting the baseline green in each — seven that must go red, and one that must stay green (a placeholder manifest status with a real failure present, proving the report-only switch); the cvdPairs assertion in gate 10; the status/icon/text triple as a TYPE, so a colour-only status fails typecheck rather than review. THREE DEFECTS FOUND IN THE APPROVED MANIFEST: (1) 37 of 38 opaque tokens had an srgb hex that did not match their own oklch, up to 6.09 dE00 — settled by ADR-0043, srgb is now engine-derived and a hand-edited hex fails the gate; (2) a DUPLICATE JSON KEY meant the top-level "status": "approved" never survived parsing, so gate.contrast.blockingWhenStatus compared against an object and the gate could never block — the pairing block is renamed statusPairing; (3) five WCAG AA failures and five CVD separation failures in the approved values, corrected in ADR-0044, whose real content is the decision to classify status.* as usage:"text" (4.5:1) rather than nonText (3:1). NOT DELIVERED: the half of gate 9 that scans RENDERED surfaces for colour-only status indicators — no component exists until F-017, and the gate prints that on every run. THE COLOUR-SCIENCE REVIEW RETURNED CHANGES REQUIRED AND FOUND FOUR REAL DEFECTS IN THE GATE, ALL FIXED: (a) the comment justifying a single severity check was FALSE — Machado is not monotone, and light status.warn/status.bad under tritan scores 61.2 at severity 0.90 against 65.8 at 1.0, so all eleven tabulated severities are now checked; (b) the separation claim was model-dependent — under Vienot total dichromacy, which color-engine.md assigns to exactly this case, light status.ok/status.warn under protan scored 59.6, BELOW the declared 60, so both models are now checked and the worse taken, and the values moved again to clear it; (c) the alpha-compositing comment was factually INVERTED — for a light overlay on a dark ground the linear reading is 2.2x more PERMISSIVE, not stricter, and the encoded model is what browsers and React Native actually draw, so both are now computed and the worse taken; (d) gate coverage was driven entirely by pairsWith, so nine tokens per theme were checked by nothing while looking exactly like tokens that passed — a token covered by nothing now fails unless it declares an uncheckedReason. ALSO CORRECTED: a wrong unit in ADR-0044 (11/255 is the encoded byte, not the linear value), the chromaCeiling field name (surfaceAndText, when the rule had become universal, was an invitation to re-derive the exemption-by-classification bug from the field name), a missing Lab-illuminant statement on ADR-0043 dE00 column, and a factually wrong comment in packages/cvd-engine/src/machado.ts claiming every reference implementation applies the matrices in encoded sRGB — R colorspace and DaltonLens apply them in linear. The palette was recomputed under BOTH conventions and clears the minimum either way (61.9 linear, 64.0 encoded), which is now recorded there. INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED on the third evaluator attempt (the first two died on session limits). The evaluation reproduced every gate green and returned FAIL on the RECORD, which no gate reads: ADR-0044 value table showed the intermediate correction rather than what shipped, and DESIGN-SYSTEM.md claimed a TypeScript brand that no code applied — TextToken/LargeTextToken were phantom brands nothing produced. Both fixed; the types are now literal unions DERIVED from the manifest usage field. It also found that NOTHING isolated checkContrast: the one contrast mutation also broke the derived-hex check, so a checkContrast returning passes:true unconditionally left gate 9 exiting 0 and all eight mutations green — verified by neutering it. Now covered by test/check.test.ts and a ninth proof case. Also fixed: turbo.json gave test:contrast no dependency on its own build; the severity-sweep decoy matched rows scoring 100 at every severity; and six stale measurements including the record of a re-measurement that was not itself re-measured. NOT REVIEWED BY A HUMAN: the corrected palette was reviewed by the designer and colour-scientist subagents, not by the person who approved it; the manifest carries a valuesChangedSinceApproval field saying so, because status:approved is the one field a gate reads. All colour maths is delegated to @irodora/color-difference and @irodora/cvd-engine, so nothing here re-implements a metric. FOUND AND RECORDED RATHER THAN FIXED: F-067 (the two themes assert opposite salience hierarchies — pre-existing), F-068 (swatch edge against an arbitrary sample), F-069 (status colour adjacent to a sample). border.strong composited over a light surface reaches 1.17:1; it is in no pairsWith so nothing checks it, and that is recorded rather than silently widened.

features.title: CVD engine and separation scoring
acceptance: Brettel-Vienot dichromacy and Machado anomalous trichromacy at severity 0 to 1
Dichromat simulation of a published confusion-line pair yields DeltaE00 below 2
One separation score in [0,100], combining post-simulation DeltaE00 with lightness difference, used identically by the UI and the recommendation engine
Gate 10 (cvd) activates
features.notes: IN PROGRESS. DELIVERED: Machado anomalous trichromacy for all three deficiencies across CONTINUOUS severity (culori snaps to 0.1 steps because its interpolation weight is Math.round(t % 0.1), always 0 — we interpolate, and the oracle is consulted only at the 11 tabulated points); Vienot dichromacy for protan and deutan; one separation score in [0,100] (E-005); gate 10 ACTIVE after being watched fail. NOT DELIVERED — acceptance criterion 1 is only partly met: TRITAN DICHROMACY. Vienot's single-plane simplification is not accurate for tritanopia, whose two half-planes diverge, so simulateDichromacy THROWS for it rather than returning a plausible wrong answer that would feed the separation score. The full two-half-plane Brettel 1997 construction is the remaining work, and there is no oracle for it in either library — the check will have to be the confusion-line property, as it is for the other two. THE BLOCKER IS IDENTIFIED AND PINNED: XYZ_TO_LMS_HPE is the WRONG fundamental set. A copunctal point is the chromaticity of the missing cone fundamental, so it is derivable from the LMS-to-XYZ columns; HPE gives tritan (0.1680, 0.0000) against the published (0.171, -0.003) — agreement to 0.003 — but protan (0.8374, 0.1626) against (0.747, 0.253) and deutan (2.3019, -1.3019) against (1.400, -0.400). The published points are Smith-Pokorny, which is also what Vienot derived from, so the remaining construction needs Smith-Pokorny fundamentals plus the four anchor stimuli (475/575 nm for protan and deutan, 485/660 nm for tritan). The fundamental set is now SETTLED: Smith-Pokorny reproduces all three published copunctal points (protan 0.0007, deutan 0.0002, tritan 0.0048). The ANCHOR STIMULI are the blocker, and an attempt was refuted rather than shipped: recalled anchors disagree with Vienot — which is the published single-plane reduction of Brettel, so a real oracle — by 32.5 dE00 (protan) and 57.4 (deutan), and the diagnostic explains why: the two half-plane normals sit 88.4 degrees apart where Vienot validity requires ~0. They cannot be derived here — computing LMS at a wavelength needs CIE colour-matching functions and there is NO spectral data in the dependency tree and no Brettel implementation to check against. FINISHING THIS NEEDS A DECISION, NOT CODE: vendor CIE colour-matching functions (a content and licensing question per content/AGENTS.md), obtain a trustworthy transcription of Brettel published anchor table, or attest criterion 1 under ADR-0038. Criterion 2 is met for protan and deutan using the kernel of the published Vienot matrix; note that pairs built from the classic published COPUNCTAL POINTS only collapse to ~5.2 dE00, because those points and Vienot's matrices come from different cone fundamentals. Recorded as a golden entry.

attested.criterion: Brettel-Vienot dichromacy and Machado anomalous trichromacy at severity 0 to 1
attested.verifiedBy: TRITAN DICHROMACY ONLY. Everything else in this criterion is gated: Machado anomalous trichromacy for all three deficiencies across continuous severity, and Vienot dichromacy for protan and deutan, are covered by gate 5 and gate 10 (ADR-0038 section 4 — where a part is checkable, that part stays gated). Tritan dichromacy needs the two-half-plane Brettel 1997 construction, which needs the LMS anchor stimuli at 485 and 660 nm. Those cannot be derived or verified here: computing LMS at a wavelength requires CIE colour-matching functions, there is no spectral data in the repository or its dependency tree, and neither culori nor colorjs.io implements Brettel. An attempt using recalled anchors was REFUTED and not shipped — it disagreed with Vienot (the published single-plane reduction of Brettel, and therefore a real oracle for protan and deutan) by 32.5 dE00 protan and 57.4 deutan, and the diagnostic showed the half-plane normals 88.4 degrees apart where Vienot validity requires ~0. DISCHARGED BY: implementing the construction against either vendored CIE colour-matching functions or a trustworthy transcription of Brettel published anchor table, and accepting only if BOTH checks pass — agreement with Vienot on protan and deutan, and near-coplanar half-plane normals. NOTE ON THE BAR: ADR-0038 asks for "verifying it requires a system we do not control". This is missing published source data rather than a missing system, which is a weaker case than a VPS or a physical device — recorded plainly rather than glossed. What makes it defensible is that tritan CVD is NOT unsupported: Machado tritanomaly is delivered across full severity and the separation score covers all three deficiencies through the Machado path, so only tritan DICHROMACY specifically is owed.

features.title: Gamut mapping
acceptance: Out-of-gamut colours map by OKLCh chroma reduction, preserving lightness and hue within stated bounds
Mapping an in-gamut colour is idempotent, asserted by property test
Golden set of known out-of-gamut colours and their mapped results
features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: gamutMap and gamutMapDetail in @irodora/color-spaces — OKLCh chroma bisection, 32 halvings, holding L and H, for sRGB and Display-P3. Zero new colour maths: every number is an existing engine conversion, and the feature is a search over a predicate. THE DECISION IS ADR-0045 AND IT IS A DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM CSS COLOR 4. The standard adds a MINDE early stop that returns the CLIPPED colour once it is within a JND in dEok, and dEok tolerates hue movement — measured against colorjs.io toGamut({method:css}) over 30 out-of-gamut colours, CSS drifts hue up to 11.97 degrees where we drift 2.6e-5, and the two results differ by up to 5.21 dE00. Our implementation was cross-checked against culori clampChroma, an independent implementation of the SAME algorithm: agreement 0.0063 dE00. The MINDE step was also structurally unavailable — dEok lives in @irodora/color-difference, which depends on this package, so implementing it would have meant a second implementation of a shipped function. Both reasons are recorded; the measurement is the one that decided it. THE STATED BOUND, which acceptance criterion 1 asks for: L and H are preserved EXACTLY in OKLCh (7e-12, the round-trip noise). After rendering, a final clamp of at most GAMUT_EPSILON=1e-7 per channel applies, and near the black point that tiny absolute movement is a large relative one — hue drift reaches 23 degrees below result L,C=0.01 where OKLCh hue is not a meaningful angle, and is 6.9e-5 degrees above L,C=0.05. Tabulated in the test rather than asserted at one convenient cutoff. THREE CASES ARE NOT CHROMA REDUCTION and each is an explicit branch: already in gamut (the early return is what makes idempotence exact), achromatic, and out of gamut in LIGHTNESS where no chroma fits and lightnessOutOfRange says so rather than a loop returning whatever it last held. THE DECOY is per-channel clipping — the algorithm almost everything else uses — implemented in the test and measured at 33.6 degrees of hue shift, with our own drift asserted beside it as the baseline. FOUND AND RECORDED, NOT FIXED: F-071, two pre-existing flaky property tests. oklab.test.ts round-trips 5000 unseeded fast-check samples against a 1e-12 bound and failed once during this feature at 1.2477e-12 before passing six consecutive full-suite runs; the F-003 evaluation found a second in packages/testing. A blocking gate that can go red for a reason unrelated to the change teaches people to re-run until green.

acceptance: Color carries required Provenance; an unclassified colour is not constructible

features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: the Color value type (canonical XYZ + required Provenance), fromXyz / fromSpace / unsafeFromHex / withProvenance, CaptureConditions, and the ReproducibilityEnvelope with a canonical serialisation and a historical replay fixture. No colour maths: this package is a facade and every conversion is @irodora/color-spaces. THE DESIGN DECISION: Provenance is a DISCRIMINATED UNION on source, not an interface with an optional conditions field. ADR-0005 says conditions is required when the source is estimated or calibrated, and an optional field only asks nicely — an estimate that lost its capture conditions would still compile, which is exactly the object nobody should be able to build. CaptureConditions was NOT invented for this: its fields are specified in docs/architecture/color-engine.md and match FR-17 (illuminant) and FR-18 (quality) exactly, so the union requires real data rather than an empty object. THE UNION BROKE THE WIRE PIN, AND THAT IS THE MECHANISM WORKING. ADR-0036 pins the engine type to the Zod schema at compile time; adding conditions turned it red immediately, which forced the contract to move in the same commit. But the union then WEAKENED the pin in a way that passed silently: keyof on a union returns only the keys COMMON to every member, so an optional field added to one member type-checked cleanly. Verified by doing it. The pin is now asserted PER MEMBER, and scripts/verify-contract-pin.mjs proves it — four probes, each adding an optional field to a different part of the schema, each asserted to turn typecheck red with the baseline asserted green first. EVERY CALL SITE IS REVIEWED, MADE COUNTABLE: scripts/verify-unsafe-call-sites.mjs enumerates unsafeFromHex call sites and runs inside pnpm lint; a new one fails the build until someone adds it to the reviewed list, which is the moment the review happens. It is a script rather than a test because the colour-engine ESLint zone forbids node: imports even in tests (NFR-3), and the alternative was weakening the strictest guard in the repository. THE REPLAY FIXTURE PINS HISTORICAL VERSIONS, not current ones, and asserts it: a fixture written from todays CORE_VERSION compares the code to itself and goes green for free. That assertion caught one of my own entries using 0.1.0.

The AUTHOR-AND-REVIEWER half is fully gated here and proven by three mutation cases (same id, same person under two ids, unknown id), as is every per-status obligation. features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: the corpus schema as a parser (@irodora/corpus), the editorial workflow and identity rule, canonical JSON and the two-level checksum, the published-version bundle with verify-at-load, scripts/generate-corpus.mjs, and GATE 11 ACTIVE AND BLOCKING with a 19-case mutation proof. 211 tests. NO COLOUR WAS ADDED — content/colors/ is still empty, which is F-012. DERIVED VALUES ARE UNAUTHORABLE, not merely regenerated: parseEntry rejects lab, lch, oklch, rgb, hex and gamut BY NAME. That is one step stronger than ADR-0043, which must regenerate-and-compare because the design manifest keeps its srgb for browsers; nothing reads a hex out of a source entry, so the stronger form was available. The rejection points at color.sourceHex, because the spec section 1 example showed those keys and an editor would have copied it. THE GATE SHIPPED BEFORE ITS DATA, which is the hard part. F-011 builds the gate and F-012 supplies the entries, so on activation the corpus is EMPTY and a gate that passes over nothing is failing open for the whole of R1. Four answers: it FAILS if it cannot locate its inputs; it runs 1 valid + 18 invalid FIXTURE corpora every invocation so the rules exercised are never zero; the fixtures cannot become content (outside content/, the scan globs content/ only, and a fixture- slug under content/ is itself a failure); and verify-content-proof.mjs mutates the VALID corpus 19 ways asserting the gate goes red AND NAMES THE RIGHT FIELD, baseline green either side, with ONE case that must stay GREEN. The authored-entry count (0) prints beside the fixture count on every run. THE CI CONDITION WAS THE WHOLE BALLGAME: gate 11 step carried `if: hashFiles(content/colors) != ''`, and gate 0 compares `run:` commands without reading `if:` — so the gate would have been "active" and never once run in CI for the rest of R1, with nothing able to say so. Removed. The general case is F-072. THREE DOCUMENTS DISAGREED about required provenance: the spec section 1 list omitted sourceLicence, publisher, rightsHolder and editorialNotes; ADR-0007 section 1 requires them and NFR-20 names the licence. The accepted decision won and the spec was corrected. IDENTITY IS A ROSTER ID (ADR-0047) because the rule was UNENFORCEABLE — the schema had no author field at all, so "author and reviewer must differ" could not run. Free text would have passed "A. Ranjan" against "Ashish Ranjan", and an UNKNOWN id must FAIL rather than count as a third person, which is the half that matters. THE REGISTER CROSS-CHECK existed only as a sentence: licensing-and-provenance.md section 5 stated the content gate performs it. It did not. Now it does, and an unparseable table is a FAILURE rather than an absence of constraint. TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY TESTS DURING THE BUILD. (1) The per-entry checksum covered only the authored record, so a tampered derived hex LOADED CLEAN and apps/api would have served it (F-016); it now covers the derived block too. (2) The bundle serialised xyz as a tuple while parseEntry requires the authored {x,y,z}, so a bundle could not load its own output. AND TWO DEFECTS THE FIXTURES FOUND IN THEMSELVES: duplicate-slug was broken in two ways and failed for the wrong rule; then, filenames coming from slugs, both entries wrote to one file and it stopped being invalid at all. Both caught by the gate, not by review — which is the argument for generating fixtures rather than hand-maintaining eighteen copies. THE HUE BOUND WAS GUESSED AND WRONG. A CIELAB bound of 6 degrees for a gamut-mapped corpus hex failed at 7.97. Measured over the six Display-P3 corners: OKLCh drift ours 0.167 vs clipping 3.150; CIELAB ours 7.966 vs clipping 5.206. IN CIELAB CLIPPING LOOKS BETTER THAN WE DO — not an algorithm failure but CIELAB and OKLab disagreeing about hue exactly where the P3 primaries sit, which is why OKLab exists. gamutMap holds OKLCh hue by construction (ADR-0045), so OKLCh is the metric that describes it; the CIELAB row is asserted as a NON-claim, because picking the flattering ruler is the failure mode here. srgbToHex moved into @irodora/color-spaces and design-tokens.toHex delegates — proven safe by 96 design-tokens tests, gate 9 and all 9 contrast mutation proofs. E-001 DESTINATION HALF IS NOW GUARDED, which it has never been: the gate recomputes every derived value in the LATEST bundle under the CURRENT engine. Older versions are checksum-verified only and the gate PRINTS that it skipped them, because asserting today's engine reproduces yesterday's answer is the claim FR-10 forbids. EVALUATION FINDINGS, FIXED IN THE SAME FEATURE. (1) E-001's rationale claimed the mutation proof watched a perturbed OKLab matrix go red. IT DID NOT — there was no such case, and the evaluator ran the experiment and watched the gate stay green. The case now exists (rebuilds color-spaces and corpus, asserts gate 11 red, restores). (2) GATE 11'S ENTIRE PUBLISHED-BUNDLE BLOCK WAS UNREACHABLE: zero real bundles until F-012, no fixture carried one, and not one proof case touched a checksum — so the charter claimed checksum and E-001 destination enforcement by code that never ran. The valid fixture corpus now carries a published version and five proof cases attack it (edited entry, edited derived value, altered ledger checksum, removed ledger row, removed entry). 25 cases now, was 19. (3) E-014 recorded guard:gate:content while the real guard was gate:test — true before the fixture had a bundle, and now genuinely both. (4) The paired memory notes for E-001 and E-006 were left stale while effects.json was updated, in direct contradiction; both rewritten. (5) OUR_OWN_CURATION was exported, documented as forcing a decision, and consumed by nothing — the rule keyed on sourceType alone, which let an editorial source call itself "traditional" or "modern-japanese". Both are claims about the received canon and neither is ours to make; the rule is now a positive list and the constant is load-bearing. (6) A test asserting CLASSIFICATIONS.filter(isOurOwnCuration) equals OUR_OWN_CURATION was true by construction and could not fail; replaced with the literal complement. ONE FINDING RECORDED RATHER THAN FIXED: the workflow STATE MACHINE (assertTransition / canTransition) has no non-test call site, so criterion 4's "draft to review to verified to published to superseded" is not enforced as a sequence. It cannot be, in a file-based corpus: there is no previous status on disk to compare a new one against. What IS enforced is every per-status obligation — a reviewer is required from `verified` onward and forbidden before it, only published|superseded enter a bundle, and author must differ from reviewer. Sequence enforcement needs stored prior state and belongs to F-062 (editorial review workflow); the machine is built and tested here so F-062 inherits it rather than reinventing it. Recorded as an attested criterion rather than claimed.

features.notes: DONE. 2026.08.1 published: 120 entries, 5 palettes, root checksum c177a55ff003c7e1cc73dda5677e5719e5ed742c02760b6a1c81963dbd3a70fb, engine 0.1.0. THE CONSTRAINT DECIDED THE FEATURE: there is no colorimeter and no cleared primary source, so sourceType can only be `editorial`, and checkClassification then permits only `japanese-inspired` or `editorial`. What was NOT already decided was the names, and ADR-0065 decides it — the seed names are Irodora coinages, not the received canon. Attaching 藍鼠 to a value that is ours would let a reader conclude the VALUE is the traditional colour’s: ADR-0007’s dishonesty pointed sideways, and easier to commit because it needs no external action. Every entry says in editorialNotes that its name is a coinage. features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: @irodora/color-naming — a Lab bucket index, a provable lower bound on ΔE00 to any box, an expanding search with a stopping rule, the ΔE00 ranking with a total comparator, the ADR-0048 similarity scale, and an adapter from a published corpus bundle. 59 tests here plus 4 in @irodora/corpus. NO CORPUS ENTRIES EXIST — F-012 is blocked on OQ-4/OQ-5 — so the suite runs on generated corpora and prints that it did. CRITERION 3 HOLDS: two-stage is byte-identical to brute force over 4,664 synthetic records x 120 adversarial queries, at four limits, at bucket steps 1/2/5/25/1e6, cross-checked against culori. MEASURED PRUNING, printed not claimed: n=45 examines 40.8%, n=416 12.9%, n=4203 2.1%. The plan warned the bound might examine ~100% at R1 sizes; it does not, and the fraction FALLS as the corpus grows. Asserted as a trend, never a threshold — a threshold at these sizes would flake and then get deleted. THE CORRECTNESS ARGUMENT IS THE FEATURE. A fixed radius — the design criterion 2 most naturally reads as — is wrong on 317 of 360 queries, first at n=45, because ΔE00 is not a metric and Lab distance does not bound it. Instead: a sound lower bound per bucket, visit in increasing bound, stop when the next cannot beat the k-th best. Correctness is then INDEPENDENT of bucket size, which the invariance test is what proves. The bound was built FIRST, out of plan order, because it was the cheapest moment to discover the algebra was wrong; four facts re-derived rather than cited, and 130k+ property samples concentrated where each could fail — plus a 200k-iteration decoy run where an unsound bound is caught and ours has zero violations. THREE THINGS TESTS FOUND THAT I HAD WRONG. (1) A property test disproved ADR-0048 on run 1: similarity is NOT strictly decreasing, because the curve is not injective in float64. The ADR now claims only monotone non-increasing — and this is an argument FOR the design, since sorting by similarity would tie where ΔE00 does not and reorder with input order. (2) The culori cross-check disagreed by 0.81 ΔE00 because culori lab is D50 and ours is D65; color-difference already calls it as lab65. A cross-check is only a check if both are asked the same question. (3) A bucket-box test assumed one bucket and got three: floor(-30/1000) is -1, so negatives land in the cell below zero. Correct behaviour, wrong expectation. A PLAN CORRECTION MADE BY typecheck IN UNDER A MINUTE: the plan specified a Color query and asserted no cycle. @irodora/color-core is the FACADE and already depends on color-naming, so depending back is a cycle by construction, and the corpus devDependency closed it again via core. The query is a Lab triple; provenance-aware wrapping belongs in the facade. The VersionBundle assignability guard moved into packages/corpus, which is the better home — the schema is that package’s contract to keep. AS A RESULT F-073 IS NOT DISCHARGED AND NOT NEEDED: the engine-to-non-engine edge does not exist rather than being contained. CRITERION 4 SHIPS HALF-GATED, declared as attested rather than discovered at the end. The structural half is enforced here — limit < 3 throws, an index of fewer than 3 records is refused, and the exact key sets of NamingCandidate and NamingResult are asserted with an exact-match-flag decoy so ADDING a field breaks the test. The lint half is F-025’s. DOCS CORRECTED: color-engine.md section 8 said "candidate retrieval from the corpus (spatially indexed for speed)" — defensible but the exact phrasing that invites the fixed radius, in a document the rules tell an implementer to read in full. It now states that retrieval is indexed and ranking cannot be, and carries the 317/360 measurement. E-003’s memory note said its consumers "do not exist yet"; that became false here and was rewritten.

features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: @irodora/color-harmony — all twelve FR-6 generators in OKLCh, every output gamut-mapped and reporting what that cost, the geometric/editorial split with attribution enforced both ways, and an adapter from a published corpus bundle. 33 tests. NO PALETTES EXIST — F-012 is blocked on OQ-4/OQ-5 — so the editorial suite runs on generated bundles and prints that it did. THE STUB WAS WRONG AGAINST ITS OWN ACCEPTANCE LIST: nine kinds where FR-6 requires twelve (missing near-neutral, warm-cool, value-contrast, chroma-contrast) AND it carried `editorial` as a KIND, which conflates two axes and makes criterion 3 unexpressible — an editorial harmony is a family, not a relationship. THE PLAN WAS ALSO WRONG, and is corrected in place: it said "an editorial harmony still stands in some relationship". Not in general — a curator assembling Quiet Neutrals is not obliged to have picked a triad, and labelling it afterwards would invent a geometric claim they never made. So `kind` is null for editorial. THE MEASUREMENT THAT JUSTIFIES THE WHOLE DESIGN. color-engine.md asserted that HSL hue rotation is perceptually inconsistent and never measured it. Over the hue circle a 30-degree HSL rotation moves the colour by ΔE00 5.0 to 35.9 — a 7.2x SPREAD. The same rotation in OKLCh ranges 9.7 to 14.5, a 1.5x spread. Asserted on the SPREAD rather than either end, because inconsistency is the claim; and OKLab is NOT asserted to be ΔE00-uniform, which would be its own over-claim. CRITERION 4 AND FR-6 PULL AGAINST EACH OTHER, AND ADR-0045 RESOLVES IT. Mapping changes a colour, so it could break the relationship just built. It does not for HUE — gamutMap holds L and h — measured here at 6.2e-5 degrees for a complementary pair and 5.3e-5 for a triad. It DOES for chroma, so chroma-contrast has a weaker tolerance and every colour reports wasGamutMapped and gamutDeltaE00. That makes E-012 a sharper link than it was: harmony depends on the PROPERTY ADR-0045 chose, not just on the function. ADR-0049: warm and cool are a stated convention anchored to the corpus taxonomy, because every other generator is derivable and this one is not — and if the engine picked its own anchors the product would contradict `taxonomy.temperature`. The ADR is blunt about the cost: two numbers cannot express a convention that varies by culture, and this product's subject is Japanese colour. PLANNED WITHOUT THE PLANNER SUBAGENT, recorded as a deviation: AGENTS.md recommends it, and it was used for F-011 and F-013 — both plans contained a factual error about this repository (F-013's asserted "no cycle" when color-core is the facade). Direct authorship after building both adjacent packages was the more reliable path here. Not a licence to skip planning: the plan exists and gate 0 enforced it.

features.notes: DONE. The corpus reaches a reader. THE ATLAS ROOT LISTS ALL 120 WITH NO FILTER, which is what makes criterion 1 checkable by walking the rendered tree rather than counting interactions by hand — a design where a family must be chosen first would make "reachable" depend on a filter set nobody enumerated. The detail screen carries all four names, every coordinate system, provenance, relations, palettes and colour vision, and it renders the FR-21 `unknowns` reason where a value is null, which is the only place those reasons mean anything. F-084’S ATTESTED CRITERION IS DISCHARGED HERE: a self-reviewed entry says "Checked by its own author" in words, asserted over the render. TWO DECISIONS IN ADR-0066. The digest function must be SYNCHRONOUS — expo-crypto is async only, and verification behind a promise can be outrun by the first render, at which point "verified at load" has become "verified shortly after we started drawing". @noble/hashes is audited and still not trusted on arrival: assertSha256 runs it against published vectors first, including 藍鼠, which catches a hasher encoding UTF-16. And the bundle ships as generated TEXT with the LEDGER’s digest beside it as two exports from two files, because a bundle checked against a checksum it carries verifies itself. WHAT THE CONFORMANCE SUITE CAUGHT WAS STRUCTURAL. The filter chips and the search box were a Pressable and a TextInput inside Atlas.tsx, where NOTHING checks them — the component suite covers the library, the screen suite covers screens as `static` subjects, and an interactive control in a screen file falls between the two. Chip and SearchField are now @irodora/ui components and the Atlas is `static`. The move immediately produced two more findings: the chips declared no minWidth (a chip is content-width, so "All" sits under 44px), and the suite’s OWN model of "interactive" was press-only, so a SearchField was reported as "nothing in the tree responds" — which would have pushed it to claim a kind it does not have. pressableNodes now counts onChangeText. That third one is the reusable lesson: when a check objects, ask whether its model is the thing that is wrong. TWO BUGS THE SOURCE CAUGHT BEFORE ANY TEST COULD. simulateDichromacy takes RGB, not XYZ — both are Triple, so passing entry.color.xyz type-checks and returns a plausible wrong colour, the same trap as handing OKLCh to ΔE00. And it THROWS for tritan by design, because VIENOT_1999 has no tritan entry and publishing one would invent a value the source does not. The block uses Machado’s simulateAnomalous at severity 1 over the bundle’s encoded sRGB, and the copy says "red-weak" rather than "protanopia" — different conditions, and the label has to match the model that produced the swatch. BOUNDARY #24 ENFORCES CRITERION 3: a screen may not import xyzTo* or gamutMap*, because recomputing a bundled value looks identical, passes every test, and returns TODAY’s engine’s answer for a version published under an older one (FR-10, E-001). srgbToHex is deliberately NOT banned — the CVD block encodes a simulated triple — and that distinction is a SILENT DECOY the rule must accept. verify-guards gained the concept and now reports overreach as its own failure with its own fix: 25 boundaries, 1 decoy. 93 NEW MESSAGE KEYS, and the existing i18n tests caught two design errors on the way in. `atlas.of` was an English sentence pattern forced onto Japanese and was DELETED rather than translated. And IDENTICAL_BY_DESIGN is capped at three deliberately, so the colour-space names became NOTATION_KEYS — a category governed by an anchored shape and a length cap instead of a longer list of favours; the ad-hoc list is now EMPTY, and its decoy caught the first shape admitting "Not recorded". E-017 FIRED A SECOND TIME, from the ja catalogue rather than the corpus: 105 uncovered codepoints of ordinary UI Japanese. The link is not only about rare kanji in colour names. E-022 IS NEW: the app reads a COPY of the bundle, so a publish without a regenerate ships a stale corpus with every gate green. Guarded by `--check` in gate 11, watched failing first. HOME NOW LINKS TO THE ATLAS. Without it the whole feature would have been the shape of a tested module nobody wired up — 120 colours, every gate green, and nothing on screen leading to any of them. F-090 (Japanese taxonomy vocabulary) and F-091 (the e2e harness) filed rather than left as comments; the Atlas shows `blue-grey` in both locales today and says so.

Palette Studio builds, edits, reorders and saves a palette to the encrypted database, and every saved palette is parsed by `parsePalette` — the same function content/palettes/*.json goes through — on the way in AND on the way back out. THAT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN: the two rules a palette EDITOR breaks are the two the schema already states (at least one anchor; ranks contiguous from 1), so a reorder bug fails at the boundary with a message that explains itself, instead of against a second copy of those rules in a screen. WHAT A DEVICE-BUILT PALETTE IS ENTITLED TO SAY ABOUT ITSELF is ADR-0067, not a decision made in passing: the corpus schema was written for provenanced editorial content and a palette built on a phone is not that, so every required field says what is actually the case — sourceId USER-LOCAL and authoredBy user-local (both RESERVED and enforced never to appear under content/), status draft so no reviewer can be recorded, versionId the corpus version it was built against, and name.en === name.ja because we do not translate user content. THE RESERVED-IDENTITY CHECK CARRIES ITS OWN DECOY, because both strings appear nowhere under content/ and a check over an empty set is indistinguishable from one that does nothing; it applies its rule to a planted record on every run, and was watched going red on a real palette before being trusted. WEIGHT IS DERIVED FROM RANK — 1.0, then a ladder from 0.9 to 0.6 — because FR-49 asks for roles and ordering and the schema requires a weight. That makes ORDER MEAN PROPORTION, which is the only reason a reorder control is worth having; it deliberately does NOT reproduce the seed palettes’ hand-authored weights, because a formula claiming to reproduce editorial judgement would be claiming something it cannot do. MIGRATION 2 adds the six columns F-041’s provisional tables could not carry, all NULLABLE WITH NO DEFAULT: a default would be a value nobody chose standing in for one somebody must, and NULL honestly means "written before this column existed" — refused by name, with the row planted through the driver because the write path cannot produce one. THE TESTS FOUND TWO REAL DEFECTS. Re-adding a removed member hit UNIQUE constraint failed, because the member lookup filtered to live rows and the derived member id collided with its own tombstone; re-adding is a RESURRECTION of that row, not a second one. And `no-role` demanded an accessibilityRole for TextInput that React Native has no name for — Role offers searchbox and no textbox, AccessibilityRole’s nearest is `text`, which means STATIC text. The checker’s model was what was wrong, so it now reads the host type, with a paired decoy proving a Pressable with no role is still reported AND that a TextInput with no NAME still is. A PRE-EXISTING RED GATE WAS FOUND AND FILED AS F-093: `pnpm test` printed 31/31 successful while --force was red in four tests. packages/store/test/key.test.ts scans apps/mobile/src for 64-hex literals and had been red since F-018 generated a bundle carrying 126 SHA-256 digests — turbo keys the task on its own package’s inputs, so a cached pass was replayed for two features. Fixed HERE, because it blocked this feature’s own verification: a 64-hex literal is an offender only if the corpus ledger does not record it, which keeps the check total instead of exempting a path, with a decoy proving a key literal is still caught. The three remaining failures are bitwise identity/golden tests failing by ULP on Node 22.16.0 against a repo pinning 24.19.0; reproduced at clean HEAD, in packages this feature does not touch, and carried by F-093. `e2e` IS IN THIS FEATURE’S VERIFICATION LIST AND WAS NOT RUN — the fourth feature to report it. Nothing declares a test:e2e task and F-091 carries it. E-017 fired a FOURTH time, for 11 codepoints; the subset was regenerated and gate 11 is green.

THE LEXICON IS VERSIONED RULE CONTENT with its own ledger (ADR-0069, ADR-0011): content/rules/phrase-lexicon.2026.08.1.json plus content/rules/index.json, two files because a record checked against a checksum it carries verifies itself. The boundaries were first round numbers, chosen from a measurement printed to three decimals. 0.40 sits a MILLIONTH above the lowest entry filed as mid — do-ma at 0.3999990449505662 — so it would have been excluded from every query for a medium colour, silently and forever. Boundaries now sit in the measured GAP: 0.395, 0.725, 0.039, 0.100. TWO DECOYS CORRECTED THE DESIGN RATHER THAN CONFIRMING IT. (1) The first vocabulary made "dark muted green" — the phrase FR-47 ITSELF NAMES — resolve to a single point matching almost nothing, because "muted" had been given grey’s range; muted is low-to-MID chroma and must overlap the hue floor or no hue can ever be muted. No anchoring fixes that, so an unprefixed hex must contain a DIGIT and `#` is how a person says they meant the colour; the cost (ffffff searches names) is asserted so it is visible rather than discovered. features.notes: DONE. A colour as a card carrying kanji, kana, romaji, English name, hex, the entry’s own classification and the corpus version. THE CRITERION DECIDED THE DESIGN. "The same entry at the same corpus version renders the same card on both platforms" is unmeetable read as "the same pixels" — iOS and Android rasterise text differently and no application code changes that, so the criterion would have become an attested-forever item and then nothing. So the card is a DOCUMENT: cardSvg() is a pure function returning SVG text, byte-identical because nothing platform-shaped touches it, and CHECKABLE IN CI WITH NO DEVICE — asserted over every entry in both themes. The rasterisation is the platform’s and is not claimed. Same move archive.ts makes for FR-58’s "byte-identical database", and ADR-0070 records it for the same reason. TEXT DOES NOT SIT ON THE SAMPLE. Putting the hex over the colour needs a legible foreground chosen per entry against 120 backgrounds with no declared pairing — inventing the contrast decision the manifest exists to make. Reusing the tokens inherits the proof; a border invented here would have inherited nothing. EVERY COLOUR IN THE DOCUMENT IS ACCOUNTED FOR — a token value or the entry’s own published hex, over all 120 entries in both themes, with a decoy proving a planted colour is reported. An SVG needs literal colours, which is what the colour-literal rule forbids in a component; the resolution is E-019’s, and E-027 records the part that is NEW: a stylesheet is rebuilt on every build and a card somebody sent last week is not. THE THUMBNAIL CLAIM IS NARROWED HONESTLY. At 96px no text on this card is comfortable. What survives is the COLOUR — the sample is 62% of the card — and the kanji, sized to clear the floor. A decoy asserts the hex and the attribution are BELOW it, because the alternative is five vague true statements instead of one sharp one. THE CONFORMANCE SUITE FOUND SOMETHING ON ITS FIRST RUN OVER THIS SCREEN: react-native-svg sets backgroundColor: transparent on its host view, and the colour-literal rule asked which token the ABSENCE of a colour is. `transparent` paints nothing, so it is now skipped — narrowly, one keyword, with a paired assertion proving a real hand-typed hex is still caught. CLASSIFICATION_KEYS IS NOW SHARED with the detail screen rather than copied. Two copies of the FR-23 vocabulary would drift, and the one that drifts would be the one on the artefact that leaves the app with none of its context. GETTING BYTES OUT IS FR-51 (R5) — no expo-sharing, no rasteriser, no device-only path — and the screen says so rather than leaving a person hunting for a share button. `e2e` IS IN THIS FEATURE’S VERIFICATION LIST AND WAS NOT RUN — the sixth feature to report it; F-091 carries gate 7. attested.criterion: Swatch-comparison flow completes in 90 seconds median, with no camera
attested.verifiedBy: THE CAMERA HALF IS GATED; THE 90 SECONDS IS NOT. "No camera" is checked over the source: no module under src/profile/ and no line of ProfileSetup.tsx matches vision-camera, expo-camera, ../lens/ or ImagePicker, with a decoy proving the scan can report one and a count proving it read the files it meant to. The DESIGN BUDGET is checked as arithmetic — 12 trials x 5 s + 20 s overhead = 80 s against FR-26 ceiling of 90 s, with a second assertion that the margin is finite so a per-trial budget of zero could not satisfy it. WHAT NO CHECK HERE REACHES: how long a real person takes. Nobody has been timed on this flow. TRIAL_BUDGET_SECONDS is a DECLARED design budget, never a measurement, and must not be quoted as one in copy or in a report (ADR-0031). "Each with its own confidence" covers all SEVEN dimensions including the three lists, which the data-model sketch did not — so the table carries seven confidence columns, and a list takes the MINIMUM of the dimensions it was derived from rather than a mean, because a mean launders a weak reading into a strong one and F-028 weights recommendations by this number. CONFIDENCE IS AGREEMENT, CAPPED AT 0.75. Unanimous 0.75, split 0.5, unanswered 0, never 1 — and the same fact produces a WIDER range when the answers disagreed, so the range and the confidence agree because they have one source. ADR-0072 records it. THE TRIALS ARE DECLARED SLUGS AND THE CLAIM LIVES IN THE BUNDLE: each pair asserts it separates on its own axis and holds the others, and test/profile.test.ts checks that against the published OKLCh trial by trial, with a decoy asserting two off-whites FAIL the same bound. A rule that refuses the obvious name and accepts the one somebody would actually type reads as coverage. WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: gate 7 (e2e) could not run — it is pending and F-091 is blocked on the environment — so no assertion here covers a cold start, real navigation, or a real gesture. attested.verifiedBy: A HELD-OUT VALIDATION RUN OVER AN ITA-STRATIFIED SAMPLE OF REAL PEOPLE, with the minimum per band stated in advance and per-band accuracy published internally. NOT DISCHARGEABLE BY ANY CHECK IN THIS REPOSITORY — it needs participants, not a fixture, and "hard to test" is explicitly not the bar for attestation; "requires a system we do not control" is, and a cohort of people is one. THE SAME CRITERION IS F-037’s THIRD, AND F-037 IS `blockedBy: [F-027]` — so the study sits downstream of the feature that creates the need for it. features.notes: DONE, with two of four criteria attested and both stated up front in the plan rather than discovered at the end — the same shape F-040 used, and for the same reason: the half that can be gated is gated and the half that needs a device or a cohort is named. Lightness from the reading’s own L, temperature from its hue, chroma from its own C — and CONTRAST ABSTAINS AT CONFIDENCE 0, because a contrast preference is the separation between two garments and one region has no second colour in it. The row reads "not asked yet", the same words a guided run uses for an unanswered trial, while every other row IS answered — which is what makes the abstention legible as a decision. A photo path that answered all seven would have invented exactly the dimension nobody would check. PHOTO_CEILING IS 0.5 AND THAT IS NOT A TUNING KNOB. It sits at or below CONFIDENCE_MAJORITY so an estimate from one reading never outranks a guided answer two of three people disagreed on, and the reason is NFR-23: nobody has measured this path across ITA° bands, so a higher number would be a claim with nothing behind it. GATE 11 CAUGHT THE COMMENT THAT EXPLAINED IT. The Japanese note saying a particular kanji is absent from the bundled face contained that kanji, so the font-coverage gate reported 441 required and one missing — the same class as the app-imports gate reading a decoy comment as an import during F-026. features.title: Personal compatibility engine
acceptance: Score in [0,100] as a pure function of profile and colour, given the rule version
Explanation objects are data: factor, contribution, direction, and an i18n message key
Per-dimension confidence weights the contribution of uncertain dimensions
No prose is generated at scoring time
features.notes: DONE, and every criterion is gated — no attestation, which is rare here and worth saying: this feature renders nothing, ships no content and touches no device, so there is no half that needs a phone or a cohort. THE SCORE IS IN [0,100] BY CONSTRUCTION RATHER THAN BY CLAMPING. It is 100 x the weighted sum of fits in [0,1], so if the weights sum to 1 the range follows — which is why `parseRuleSet` REFUSES anything else instead of the engine clamping. A clamp would turn a defect in the weights into a plausible number at the boundary, which is the same failure shape as an accuracy claim with nothing behind it. The tolerance is 1e-9 because 0.4+0.3+0.2+0.1 is 0.9999999999999999 and a validator that rejected the most obvious weight set anybody would write is a validator somebody deletes. CRITERION 3 IS THE RENORMALISATION, AND THE DECOY IS WHAT PROVES IT. effective weight = weight x confidence, DIVIDED BY THEIR TOTAL. Without the division an uncertain profile simply scores every colour lower — which reads as "this suits you less" when the truth is "we know less about you", and those are different claims. The test halves every confidence and asserts THE SCORE DOES NOT MOVE, and separately that silencing a dimension the colour MISSES on raises the score while silencing one it MATCHES on lowers it. A single direction would also be produced by an implementation that just scaled everything down. NO PROSE, AND NO DEFAULT RULE SET. The engine emits `explain.<factor>.<direction>` keys and holds no catalogue, locale or formatter — a sentence produced at scoring time has to be translated at scoring time, and a stored recommendation becomes a stored English string. And there is deliberately NO `DEFAULT_RULES` export: a default would be a weight living in code, in the one place F-029 would have to find it, and E-009 would be false the day it was written. `scoreColor` requires a RuleSet; the tests build their own. FIFTY IS AN ANSWER, NOT A FALLBACK. With every confidence at zero there is nothing to renormalise, so the engine returns 50 with confidence 0 and all four contributions at zero — legibly "nothing to go on". Not equal weights, which would assert certainty the profile does not have. F-027 makes this reachable rather than theoretical: a photo estimate abstains on contrast at confidence 0. THE PROFILE ARRIVES STRUCTURALLY. `PersonalProfile` is a shape `NewPersonalProfile` satisfies, so the engine never imports `@irodora/store` — and because the two meet NOWHERE in the product yet, `test/profile.test.ts` is currently the only place a column removed in the store would fail. It is a devDependency import for exactly that reason. THE LOCKFILE GATE F-098 BUILT PAID FOR ITSELF WITHIN THE HOUR. Adding @irodora/color-spaces and @irodora/store to this package’s manifest failed gate 0 immediately, naming both packages and both sections, BEFORE any install — which is what it was built to do for somebody who cannot run pnpm at all. The matching three-line importer entries were written by hand and gate 0 confirmed the pair agrees. WHAT IS NOT PROVEN AND IS RECORDED AS E-032: `hueBias` here and `biasFromHue` in apps/mobile/src/profile/photo.ts are two implementations of one colour rule, carried with `guard: none` because the app cannot depend on this package until pnpm install can run. Two guards were considered and rejected as models that would report green while the algorithms drifted. F-099 deletes the duplicate. NOTHING CONSUMES THIS ENGINE YET — F-030 is what will, and it is blocked on F-029.

features.title: Rule and weight content system
acceptance: Weights and harmony rules are versioned, immutable content in content/rules
Every rule carries a rationale; a weight without one cannot be published
Weights sum to 1.0, validated at publish time
Changing a weight changes rankings with no deployment
Occasion contexts are deterministic weighting profiles
features.notes: DONE, and it CLOSES E-009 — the longest-standing owed check in the graph, carried with `guard: none` since 2026-08-13. Every criterion is gated; no attestation. THE WORD THAT MATTERED IN E-009 WAS "SILENTLY". A weight file that does not sum to 1 still parses as JSON, still carries five occasions, and still produces a number for every colour — one that cannot be compared with a number from any other context. Nothing downstream throws, so nothing downstream could ever have been the guard. THE GATE DOES NOT RE-IMPLEMENT THE RULE. `verify-content.mjs` loads the BUILT @irodora/recommendation and calls `parseWeightContent`, which wraps F-028’s own `parseRuleSet` — so "these weights normalise" is decided by the code that SCORES with them rather than by a copy in a script that would agree on the day it was written (E-013). A `loadRecommendationPackage` sits beside `loadCorpusPackage` for exactly that reason, and criterion 3 was therefore already half-built before this feature started. WATCHED FAILING IN BOTH HALVES, ON THE REAL PUBLISHED FILE. A weight moved from 0.35 to 0.9 reports "occasions.default: weights sum to 1.5499999999999998, not 1". A SINGLE WORD changed in a rationale — a file that still parses perfectly, and which the sum check cannot see — reports a digest that does not match the ledger. The second is the immutability half of ADR-0011 and it needed its own mutation, because the first throw short-circuits the rest of the block. Restored byte-exactly afterwards, proven by the digest passing again rather than by reading a diff. AN OCCASION IS A WEIGHT SET, which is why FR-34 cost almost nothing. `scoreColor` already took a RuleSet, so choosing a context is choosing which one to pass. The alternative — an occasion as a modifier applied AFTER scoring — would have put a second set of numbers between the weights and the answer, and the weights would have stopped being the thing that decides. CRITERION 4 IS THE ONE A TEST CAN MOST EASILY FAKE. "Changing a weight changes rankings" is satisfied by asserting two numbers differ, which would pass on an engine that read no weights and returned noise. It is asserted as a REORDERING of the same colours through an engine that is byte-identical between the two calls, plus a check that the same occasion always produces the same order — and a third that connects the numbers to the PROSE: the japanese-inspired rationale claims restraint is a chroma property, so a colour outside the chroma tolerance must score worse there than under casual and better under formal, which carries the lowest chroma weight. Without that a rationale could say anything at all. THE FIRST DRAFT OF THAT TEST WAS WRONG AND THE FAILURE WAS INSTRUCTIVE: it asserted rank POSITION, and the vivid colour sits third under both occasions because the colours above it move too. Rank is a comparison against whichever candidates happen to be in the list; the SCORE is what the weight acts on and what the rationale is a claim about. A SECOND FAILURE IMPROVED THE PARSER. features.title: Backup, export and import — the durability story
acceptance: An export contains every record, tombstones included, and re-imports to an identical canonical digest of every row of every table
Erasure is immediate and local: every table hard-deleted, change_log included, and the key destroyed so bytes already on disk stay unreadable
A re-query against each store returns nothing; the return value of the erase call is not the proof

attested.criterion: The export and import journeys complete on a device, writing to and reading from a file the person chose
attested.verifiedBy: A device run of the export and import flows against a real file, on iOS and Android. The MECHANISM is gated here — the round trip, every refusal, and the ordering are all tested in Node against the node:sqlite driver — but file access is behind the ArchiveSink interface precisely so the package needs no platform to be tested, which means the platform binding itself is what a device confirms. FR-58 says "asserted in e2e"; pnpm test:e2e exits 1 by design while no surface declares the script, and gate 7 activates with F-018/F-040.

features.notes: DONE. With no server this is the entire durability story (ADR-0051 section 5), which is why it is a first-release feature and not a follow-up. 27 tests in @irodora/store. "BYTE-IDENTICAL" IS INTERPRETED, IN THE OPEN. Taken literally FR-58 is unmeetable: a SQLite FILE differs in page layout, freelist state and AUTOINCREMENT sequence after an identical sequence of writes, so no import could ever satisfy it and the criterion would eventually be softened quietly instead of deliberately. The claim worth making is that the DATA round-trips, so digest() is a canonical serialisation — every table in a declared order, every row INCLUDING TOMBSTONES, every column sorted — and that is compared byte for byte, against the ORIGINAL database rather than against the archive it came from. Comparing an export to an export is an echo that passes on an exporter dropping the same column twice. THE ARCHIVE IS JSON, NOT A FILE COPY: a copy of an encrypted database is useless without the key, and shipping the key with the backup makes the encryption theatre. The stated cost is that the archive is plaintext — readable by the user, which is the point, and by anyone who obtains it, which is the price. Recorded as a decision rather than discovered later. THE LINT FOUND A DESIGN FLAW: importArchive typed its parameter as Archive, and no-unnecessary-condition flagged the format check as always-false — which is exactly the type asserting a fact about data nobody had checked. An archive arrives from a FILE the user chose. It now takes `unknown` and validates every field, and distinguishes a MISSING table (an older archive, accepted as empty) from one present but not an array (corruption, refused) — treating them alike would import garbage as emptiness. TWO REFUSALS THAT SEPARATE A RESTORE FROM A DISASTER: a NEWER schemaVersion is refused rather than guessed at, the same rule migrate() applies; and a non-empty database is refused rather than merged, because a silent merge duplicates everything a user owns and looks like it worked. ERASURE IS PROVEN BY RE-QUERY, and eraseEverything RETURNS VOID so the test FR-58 warns against cannot be written. Its decoy is the one that matters: a "wipe" that only tombstoned would leave every row on disk while every list came back empty — soft delete exists so a sync can tell "deleted" from "never existed", and erasure exists so nothing remains to tell anything about. Destroying the key is what makes it true of bytes already written; a file delete leaves recoverable blocks and a row-by-row delete leaves them too. THE ORDER IS THE WHOLE FEATURE. eraseWithBackupPrompt enforces offer -> write -> confirm -> erase in code, so a caller cannot get it wrong by writing the calls in the order that reads more naturally, and the test asserts the ORDER rather than the outcome — a test checking only "a backup exists and the data is gone" passes on an implementation that erased first and backed up an empty database. AND THE CASE THAT MATTERS MOST: if a requested export FAILS, nothing is erased. Losing the data and the backup in one action is the worst outcome available here, and it is exactly what a try/catch that carries on produces.

The limit is carried as DATA, not as a comment: the Node driver reports encryptsAtRest:false, the suite prints which driver it ran, and a test asserts it, so a green CI run cannot be read as a statement about encryption. PRAGMA foreign_keys IS THE SUBJECT OF THE SUITE. SQLite defaults it OFF and it is PER CONNECTION, so a schema full of REFERENCES enforces nothing unless it runs every time — it looks right in the DDL and accumulates orphans in silence. The check watches a bad write FAIL rather than reading the pragma back, and writing that test found the trap underneath it: PRAGMA foreign_keys IS A NO-OP INSIDE A TRANSACTION, so the first mutation (turning it off after the user_version bump, inside the migration transaction) changed nothing and the test failed for an unrelated reason. THREE ASSERTIONS WRITTEN AGAINST TESTS THAT LOOK RIGHT AND PROVE NOTHING: durability REOPENS the database, and the driver refuses reopen() on :memory: with a message saying why, because a round-trip without a reopen tests the cache; the change log is checked for WHICH row and op in WHICH order, never for a count; and a rolled-back transaction must leave NO change-log row, because a log entry describing a write that did not happen would be applied confidently by a future reconciler. THE KEY LIFECYCLE IS BEHIND AN INTERFACE BECAUSE IT IS THE PART NO DEVICE WOULD REVEAL: a key regenerated on every launch encrypts a database nobody can open again, which presents as "the app lost my data" — reported once, months later, unreproducible. It is a two-line test here. Its decoy is the one that matters: a CONSTANT key would satisfy "same on second call" perfectly and would be a key every user shares. keyPragma refuses anything that is not 64 hex characters, because PRAGMA takes no bound parameter and the key is interpolated. A test scans shipped source for a 64-hex literal, excluding test files by path. THE GUARD NO TEST COULD REPLACE: apps/mobile bundles this package, so a node:sqlite import reachable from src/index.ts is a crash on a phone and is invisible to every gate — the tests run in Node, where it resolves perfectly. The Node driver is behind @irodora/store/node and src/drivers/node.ts is exempted by explicit path, never by glob. Guard 15, planted and watched firing. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: Drizzle, which ADR-0051 section 2 names — it is a query builder over a driver, and adding it before the repository interface existed would have settled the interface by accident. Recorded as a follow-up rather than a silent omission. And change_log is written and read by NOTHING: ADR-0051 section 6 is explicit that it is not an outbox, because an outbox implies a destination and a delivery guarantee.

attested.criterion: The database is actually encrypted at rest, and a write survives a force-quit mid-transaction
attested.verifiedBy: Running apps/mobile/src/store/conformance.ts on a physical device, then inspecting the database file for SQLite header bytes — an unencrypted file begins with "SQLite format 3", an encrypted one does not. SQLCipher is not in node:sqlite, so NOTHING in CI says anything about encryption at rest; the Node driver reports encryptsAtRest:false and a test asserts it, so a green CI run cannot be mistaken for this. The force-quit case needs a real process kill mid-transaction, which is why PRAGMA synchronous is FULL rather than NORMAL. The attestation is one call rather than a day of work because the same checkStore the CI driver runs is already wired to the device driver.

attested.criterion: SQLite behind one repository interface with a conformance suite that both drivers run — node:sqlite in CI, expo-sqlite on the device
attested.verifiedBy: The CI half is gated: node:sqlite runs all seven checks every build. features.title: Cross-theme salience hierarchy for the status tokens, and the APCA floor for dark error
acceptance: The salience rank of status.ok, status.warn and status.bad against each theme own ground is the same in both themes
