features.title: A design token that reaches no component fails a check
acceptance: Every value emitted from the design manifest is either read by a component or declared unreached with a reason
A token whose only reader is its own emitter test is reported by name
Proven by removing a real consumer and watching the check name that token
A deliberately unreached token can be declared, in the same visible-and-reasoned shape as retired-ok
features.notes: DONE. Every value in packages/design-tokens/src/generated/ was already byte-compared against the manifest TWICE — by emit.test.ts and by generate-design-tokens.mjs --check — so each one was known to be CORRECT. Nothing anywhere asked whether it was USED. scripts/verify-token-reach.mjs now runs in gate 8 beside a11y-scope.mjs: of 71 emitted names, 37 are read by a component and 34 are declared unreached with a reason. ADR-0071. THIS IS ADR-0054 ONE LEVEL DOWN. A component nobody renders and a token nobody paints are the same defect, and only one was reported — a cost paid twice already, by F-019 finding nativeNumericFeature by hand and F-094 finding the same shape at artefact level. THREE RULES DECIDE WHETHER IT IS WORTH ANYTHING. (1) packages/ui/src/testing/ is NOT a reader: a token read only by the conformance checker exists so a CHECK can enforce it, and without that exclusion four findings vanish and acceptance criterion 2 is unsatisfiable by construction. (2) Reach propagates through OBJECT VALUES (Surface resolves surface.1 through nativeElevation, and that name appears nowhere as a literal) but never through KEYS (theme.tsx reads nativeColors, whose keys are all 33 colour tokens) and never through ARRAY ELEMENTS (a membership test is a question nobody answers with the token). An object is looked up; a list is looked in. (3) COMMENTS ARE NOT CODE. THE PROOF FOUND THE BUG, NOT THE READING. border.strong was removed from all five components that use it and the check still called it reached, because Button.tsx mentions it in BACKTICKS in a comment explaining why it does not pair — and a backtick is one of the quote characters a literal read matches. Every JSDoc example in a repository that comments this heavily was counting as a consumer. Stripping comments turned three more tokens honest, the best of them foreground.3: THE TOKEN WHOSE ENTIRE PURPOSE IS TO BE RESTRICTED IS PAINTED BY NOTHING, and every mention of it in the reader zone is prose about why it is dangerous. Two more the prototype got wrong: nativeRadius.pill is a MEMBER ACCESS, not a literal, so the first version reported every radius step in the product as unreached; and xs is a radius step AND a type step, so 22 size="xs" literals were marking the radius reached. A name in two groups is now resolvable only from an owner- or prop-scoped read. THE ALLOWLIST IS THE ARTEFACT. .harness/verification/unreached-tokens.json is a readable inventory of what the design system has DRAWN and the product has not yet BUILT — no chart, no dialog or bottom sheet, no animation, no display type on any screen, and a Status component that conforms and that no screen renders. Every entry cites the feature that will consume it; the whole list prints on EVERY run, not only on a failure; and a declaration for a token that IS read fails, the same both-directions rule as E-021 and E-028. ONE ENTRY IS A DEFECT AND IT IS FILED AS F-095: nativeSpacing is emitted, exported and imported by nothing, while 69 hand-written padding/margin/gap declarations use eight values of which FIVE ARE NOT ON THE SCALE and 1, 2, 6 are not even multiples of the declared base: 4. An escape hatch whose reason is a pointer to work is working; one whose reason is a soothing sentence is how a defect becomes permanent. NO FILE IN packages/, apps/ OR content/ CHANGED. This feature adds a check and writes down what it found; it does not move a pixel. The proof plants IN MEMORY, so nothing is written to the working tree. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER: a reader is found by string literal, which is a heuristic and not a type — a component that built a token name by concatenation would be reported as unreached, the false positive that gets a check deleted; none exists today and the header says which way it errs. Leaf level reaches named tokens only, so nativeMotion.durations.micro is not individually checked.

features.title: A cached task result is replayed for a world that changed
acceptance: A task whose test reads a file outside its own package is invalidated when that file changes
A cached result produced under a different Node or pnpm version is not replayed
The failure is demonstrated before the fix: a planted change outside a package must turn its cached green red
features.notes: DONE. `pnpm test` printed "31 successful, 31 total — 26 cached" while --force was red in four tests. It now prints "23 successful, 31 total" over the same repository state, which is the whole feature: the red was always there and the cache was reporting over it. BOTH FAILURES WERE DEMONSTRATED BEFORE BEING FIXED. H1: planting a manifest change that fails seven design-tokens tests (radius.swatch 0 -> 4) produced "cache hit, replaying logs — 5 successful, 5 total"; with the manifest in globalDependencies the same change produced "cache miss, executing" and three red suites. H2: `turbo run test --dry=json` shows the global hash carrying `.nvmrc` as a GIT BLOB and `engines` as a RANGE — the file that REQUESTS a version and a range, neither of which is the runtime — so nothing in it varies with the Node executing. After the fix, the same toolchain twice is a cache hit and a different IRODORA_TOOLCHAIN value is a miss with a different hash. THE TWO HOLES GOT DIFFERENT FIXES BECAUSE THEY ARE DIFFERENT IN KIND. The manifest is a small central artefact that legitimately belongs to the whole repository, so it joined globalDependencies beside tsconfig.base.json. `apps/mobile/src` is not: putting it there would invalidate all 31 tasks on any app edit, and a cache people distrust is a cache people turn off. So the FR-56 key scan MOVED OUT of packages/store/test/key.test.ts into verify-no-key-material.mjs — uncached, in gate 15, which is requiredFor:always rather than requiredFor:code. A REPOSITORY-WIDE CHECK DOES NOT BELONG INSIDE ONE PACKAGE’S TEST SUITE, not because caching is awkward to configure but because the scope of the question and the scope of the cache key disagree by construction and nothing reports that. Moving it widened the scan to every shipped src/ and immediately found four more legitimate 64-hex literals — the FIPS 180-4 vectors in corpus/digest.ts — now accounted for by EXACT VALUE, never by path, because exempting the file would let a key be pasted beside them. THE DURABLE DELIVERABLE IS verify-cache-scope.mjs, because fixing two instances does not stop the third. Two rules: a test may not read past its package unless the target is a declared global dependency (an unresolvable path counts as unaccounted — failing closed), and a cached task must be started by scripts/gate.mjs. Rule 1 proven with --prove over 6 planted cases including two controls, baseline green either side; rule 2 watched going red on a script reverted to a bare `turbo run test`. THE PROOF NEEDED A SECOND ATTEMPT and that is recorded: the first plant sat one directory deeper than a real test, so every planted ascent landed back INSIDE the package and three cases reported "nothing" while looking like a broken scanner. The first scanner draft was also wrong in the same way — it used a fixed count of ".." and reported ten in-package golden fixtures as escapes; ascents are resolved against the file’s real position now, with one level of base indirection because `const PACKAGE = join(HERE, "..")` is how the real case is written. ADR-0068 records the decision NOT to refuse on a mismatched toolchain: a false red is unhelpful, a false green is a gate lying about the code, and keying removes the second completely — refusing would add nothing to that while leaving a workstation unable to run any gate at all. THE TEST GATE IS NOW RED ON THIS WORKSTATION and that is correct: Node 22.16.0 cannot reproduce fixtures pinned to the last bit, F-083 says in as many words not to regenerate them, and the single blocking action is a Node upgrade — which no repository change can perform. ALSO FOUND, NOT FIXED, FILED AS F-094: `generate-design-tokens.mjs --check` exists, is referenced in two plans as "the freshness check", and is wired into no gate and no CI step.

features.title: The token generator has a --check nobody runs
acceptance: A stale generated token module fails a gate rather than shipping
The check is watched failing on a manifest edited without regenerating
features.notes: DONE, AND SMALLER THAN IT WAS FILED AS — the measurement corrected the premise. `generate-design-tokens.mjs --check` now runs FIRST in gate 9, so a manifest edited without regenerating, or a generated artefact edited by hand, fails before the suites that would agree with the stale values. THE FILED CLAIM WAS THAT ALL FIVE GENERATED ARTEFACTS WERE UNGUARDED. That was wrong. `packages/design-tokens/test/emit.test.ts` already byte-compares FOUR of them — tokens.css, tokens.tailwind.css, tokens.ts and native.ts — and carries its own "checks all four targets" assertion, so a stale manifest already failed gate 5. Planting a manifest edit and watching gate 5 go red is what established that, rather than reading the plan back to myself. THE REAL HOLE WAS ONE ARTEFACT, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT SHIPS: apps/mobile/global.css, the app’s own stylesheet. Measured, not inferred — hand-editing a hex in it leaves ALL 172 design-tokens tests green, and only the new check reports it. That file is E-019’s own subject, and E-019’s guard names heroui.test.ts and emitHeroui throwing, neither of which compares the committed file against what the manifest would emit now. WATCHED FAILING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which fail differently and are worth telling apart: an edited MANIFEST reports the derived srgb field plus four files at once; an edited ARTEFACT reports exactly one. Baseline asserted green either side of each, and the first mutation attempt SILENTLY DID NOT APPLY — `oklch` is an object, not an array — which is why every plant here throws if the value it meant to change did not change [[a-decoy-that-is-not-broken-proves-nothing]]. E-007 now names all five artefacts including global.css and tokens.tailwind.css, its guard names both halves, and its memory note no longer says "the four outputs" — the gap between "four" and "five" WAS the defect. No source changed: this feature is wiring plus proof.

features.title: The spacing scale reaches a component, or the value is not on the scale
acceptance: Every padding, margin and gap value in packages/ui/src and apps/mobile/src comes from the spacing scale, or is declared off-scale with a reason
nativeSpacing is imported by at least one component, so the emitted scale has a reader
A hand-written value that is not a step of the scale fails a check that names the file and the value
The five values in use today that are NOT on the scale — 1, 2, 6, 12, 16 — are each either moved onto it or added to it by an ADR
features.notes: FOUND BY F-092, not by inspection. `nativeSpacing` (4, 8, 14, 20, 28, 40, 56, 96) is emitted from the manifest, exported from @irodora/design-tokens, and IMPORTED BY NOTHING — its only reader is emit.test.ts. Meanwhile there are 69 hand-written padding/margin/gap declarations across packages/ui/src and apps/mobile/src using 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16 and 20, and 36 OF THE 69 USE A VALUE THE SCALE DOES NOT CONTAIN. So the manifest declares a rhythm the product does not follow, and nothing noticed because nothing was looking. WHY THIS IS ITS OWN FEATURE AND NOT PART OF F-092: moving 69 values changes layout on every screen, and five of the eight values in use are not decisions the manifest ever made — so the work is a design decision (does 16 become 14 or does the scale gain 16?) before it is a refactor. F-092 recorded it rather than excusing it, and .harness/verification/unreached-tokens.json cites this id as the reason nativeSpacing is declared unreached. THE 4-BASE MATTERS: the manifest says `spacing.base: 4`, and 1, 2, 6 are not multiples of it, so those three are off-grid rather than merely off-scale. A screenshot or device comparison before and after is worth more here than a test, because the failure mode is "the layout is now subtly wrong everywhere".

features.title: The key-material scan has no ledger for a rules digest
acceptance: verify-no-key-material.mjs accounts for the rules-bundle digest and gate 15 is green with no shipped source unexplained
A planted 64-hex literal that is NOT a recorded digest is still reported, proven by a decoy
features.notes: FOUND WHILE VERIFYING F-026, PRE-EXISTING, AND CONFIRMED AT HEAD WITH EVERY F-026 CHANGE STASHED. `node scripts/verify-no-key-material.mjs` reports apps/mobile/src/rules/generated/lexicon.ts carrying 64 hex digits "the ledger does not record", and exits 1 — so gate 15 (security) is RED. The literal is not a key: `git grep` finds the same value in content/rules/index.json, which is the rules bundle digest F-069 introduced. The script accounts for CORPUS digests by reading content/versions/ (130 of them), and the rules bundle is a second versioned artefact with its own digest home that the script has never been taught about. THE FILE WAS LAST WRITTEN BY F-021 (f0f1f6c), so this has been red since then; the sessions after it recorded gate 15 as "partly run" because gitleaks was not installed and did not report the key scan failing — which is how a red gate stayed invisible across four features. That second-order lesson is the reason this is `should` and not `could`. FIX SHAPE: the ledger the script consults should be every recorded digest, not every corpus digest, and the decoy in the fix must plant a 64-hex literal that is NOT a recorded digest — otherwise widening the ledger is indistinguishable from switching the check off. DONE. THE FIX IS THE ONE THE NOTE ABOVE PREDICTED: `ledgerDigests()` now reads a NAMED list of content ledgers — content/versions/ (126 digests) and content/rules/index.json (1) — rather than the corpus ledger alone, and gate 15 is green over 179 shipped source files with nothing unexplained. THE DECOY WAS THE PART WORTH GETTING RIGHT. The existing probe took `[...ledger][0]`, which is one of the four published SHA-256 vectors hard-coded in this script — it is silent whether or not either ledger FILE was read, so it could never have caught the rules ledger being absent from the list, which is exactly the defect. There is now one probe PER LEDGER SOURCE, each using the first digest that source carries, plus the planted key literal that must still be reported. A named ledger that is missing, or that records no checksum at all, now FAILS rather than contributing nothing: absence makes this check STRICTER, which is the safe direction and therefore precisely the kind of breakage nobody investigates — until the day it is easier to silence a real finding than to work out why the ledger went quiet. Each source prints its digest count on every run for the same reason. PULLED FORWARD FROM R3 DELIBERATELY, and this is the one place release order gives way: gate 15 was RED at HEAD and gate 15 is blocking. A red blocking gate is not a scope choice to be sequenced. WATCHED FAILING, four ways, each restored and the baseline green after: dropping content/rules/index.json from LEDGER_SOURCES reproduces the original finding on lexicon.ts exactly; a missing ledger file and a ledger recording nothing each fail naming the source; and the planted key literal is still reported on every run. THE SECOND-ORDER LESSON IN THE NOTE ABOVE HELD AGAIN. This was found only because `pnpm install` finally ran here and gate 15 could be executed in full — it had been red since F-021 (f0f1f6c) and CI never reached it, because CI stopped at the install step (see F-098).

features.title: The photo path has no producer: a capture surface hands a reading to profile setup
acceptance: A capture surface exists that a person can reach, and it produces a LensReading
Profile setup receives that reading from the surface rather than from a prop a test supplies
A person can complete photo-assisted setup end to end without a test harness
features.notes: FILED BY F-027, WHICH BUILT THE CONSUMER. `estimateFromReading` is checked twelve ways and is reachable in the app only by passing a `LensReading` in as a prop — nothing constructs one. That is [[a-tested-module-nobody-wired-up-passes-every-test-it-has]] exactly, and it is recorded rather than absorbed because F-027’s criteria are about the ESTIMATE and the CONFIRMATION, and widening them to build a viewfinder would have been scope nobody reviewed against a requirement. THE GAP IS OLDER THAN F-027: F-040 is `done` and shipped `read()` plus four capture modes wired to nothing, with its four device criteria attested — so the app has had a capture seam and no capture surface since R2. This feature is the surface. WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY PART OF F-040: F-040 is closed and its attestations describe the frame-processor behaviour on a device, which is a different claim from "a person can reach this". NOTE THE VERIFICATION REALITY BEFORE CLAIMING IT: a VisionCamera surface cannot be rendered by jest, so the a11y conformance registry cannot hold it in the shape the other eight screens use, and criterion 3 needs gate 7 — which is pending on F-091.

features.title: The lockfile drifts from a manifest and only the install step finds out
acceptance: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile succeeds at HEAD on the pinned toolchain
A manifest declaring a dependency the lockfile does not resolve fails gate 0 — before install — naming the package and the workspace project
A changed specifier, a removed dependency, an override drift and a workspace project with no importer each fail the same check
The check is watched failing, and watched STAYING GREEN on a reformatted manifest and on a workspace project that declares nothing
features.notes: FILED AFTER THE FACT AND SAYING SO. CI was red on three consecutive pushes (4528c52, bfcfe9d, dfc3239) at the `Install` step, with all seventeen steps after it skipped. This was not selected through next-feature; it was diagnosed from a red build and repaired, and the record is written to match what happened rather than to look like the loop. ROOT CAUSE: F-020 (9ce0926) added `@irodora/corpus: workspace:*` to packages/store/package.json and nothing regenerated pnpm-lock.yaml, so `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` refused with ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE naming that one package. IT WAS NOT CARELESSNESS, WHICH IS WHY A GATE IS THE RIGHT ANSWER: `pnpm install` could not run on the workstation at all (Node 22.16.0 and pnpm 9.3.0 against engines demanding 24.19.0 and 11), and progress.md records the workaround honestly — packages/store/node_modules/@irodora/corpus was a hand-made junction. The junction made the local tree behave correctly, and there was no local command that could have disagreed with it. FIXED by regenerating the lockfile on the pinned toolchain; the diff is three lines, the importer entry that was missing. GUARDED by a new section in gate 0 that mirrors pnpm own rule — the same three dependency sections, the same verbatim specifier comparison, the same overrides handling — and runs BEFORE install, on Node built-ins, on a clean clone. That last part is the whole point: it is the only place that can say "the lockfile is stale" to somebody who cannot run pnpm at all. Workspace projects come from the pnpm-workspace.yaml globs rather than a hard-coded list, and a glob the parser cannot expand FAILS rather than being skipped. PROVEN by scripts/verify-lockfile-proof.mjs, wired into CI beside the other gate 0 proofs: seven cases with the baseline green either side, five red and TWO GREEN. The second control is the one that matters — a workspace project declaring nothing is written `tests/bench: {}` in the lockfile, and reading that as absent would have made the check fail on a correct lockfile from its first run. FOUND WHILE FIXING THIS, and fixed under its own id: gate 15 was independently red at HEAD (F-096). Repairing install alone would have moved the red from step 9 to step 25.

features.title: One warm/cool rule: the app imports the engine instead of repeating it
acceptance: apps/mobile/src/profile/photo.ts computes no warm/cool bias of its own and imports the engine
The reference poles reach the app from the same rule set the engine scores with, not from a literal
E-032 is resolved, and gate 0 stops warning that it carries no guard
features.notes: FILED BY F-028, WHICH WROTE THE SECOND COPY AND SAID SO. `hueBias` (engine) and `biasFromHue` (app) compute the same thing with the same constants, two features apart. E-008 states the consequence: a second implementation makes the same input measure differently on two surfaces and no single-platform test can see it — both sides pass their own tests today. THE DRIFT HAS A PREDICTABLE DIRECTION, which is the part worth knowing: the engine’s poles are a RULE SET field, so F-029 will version them as content, while the app’s are literals. The first time an editor moves the warm pole, a profile built from a photograph will disagree with the score the engine gives it, with every gate green. BLOCKED ON THE TOOLCHAIN, NOT ON A DECISION: the one-line fix is an import, and apps/mobile/node_modules/@irodora/ has no `recommendation` link because `pnpm install` refuses on Node 22.16.0 against engines demanding 24.19.0. Adding the dependency ALSO needs the lockfile importer entry, which gate 0 now checks (F-098) — so the manifest and lockfile half is mechanical and verifiable here; it is the node_modules link that is not, and a hand-made junction is what F-098’s own notes call the workaround that hid a stale lockfile for four features. DO IT ON THE PINNED TOOLCHAIN.

features.title: A proof that perturbs the colour engine and cannot put it back
acceptance: verify-content-proof.mjs leaves packages/color-spaces/src/matrices.ts unmodified however it exits
On a toolchain that cannot rebuild, it refuses BEFORE mutating anything and says why
The restore is unconditional rather than dependent on the mutation succeeding
features.notes: FILED AFTER THE FACT AND SAYING SO — found while verifying F-029, not selected through next-feature. THE DEFECT: the E-001 case in verify-content-proof.mjs writes a perturbed OKLab matrix into packages/color-spaces/src/matrices.ts and then calls `rebuild()`, which shells out to pnpm. On this workstation pnpm refuses outright — Node 22.16.0 against engines >=24.19.0 — so `apply()` THREW AFTER THE WRITE, the throw escaped before the case’s `cleanup` could run, and the script exited leaving a corrupted colour engine in a TRACKED SOURCE FILE. WHAT THAT LOOKS LIKE FROM THE OUTSIDE: gate 11 goes from green to 374 failures, every one reading "the CURRENT engine derives ... publish a NEW corpus version". The diff is ONE DIGIT — 0.819022437996703 became 0.829022437996703 — in a file nobody in the session had opened. I spent a long time bisecting my own changes for it, because a corrupted engine looks exactly like a feature that broke the corpus. `git status` naming matrices.ts as modified was what finally said otherwise. THE REAL DANGER IS THE COMMIT. The perturbation is a tracked-file edit that `git add -A` picks up without comment, so the next feature commit made on this workstation after running the proof would have shipped a wrong colour matrix — the one artefact in this repository whose corruption changes every derived value and reproduces perfectly. TWO FIXES, BOTH NEEDED. (1) `apply` and `runGate` are now inside a try/FINALLY so cleanup is unconditional — the case’s own cleanup does `git checkout` BEFORE its rebuild, so the source comes back even when the rebuild then throws. (2) The proof RUNS `rebuild()` ONCE UP FRONT, on an unmodified tree, and exits naming the toolchain if it fails — refusing before mutating rather than discovering it halfway through. A proof that perturbs a colour matrix and then reports an unrelated failure is a proof nobody can read. WATCHED: the proof now exits 1 with "This proof cannot run on this toolchain", `git status packages/color-spaces/` is empty afterwards, and gate 11 stays green. What is NOT proven here is that the proof still DISCRIMINATES — that needs the pinned toolchain, and it was already the case before this change that nobody on Node 22 could run it.

features.title: A near-neutral has no temperature, everywhere it is judged
acceptance: Every place a colour of arbitrary chroma is judged for warmth reads a chroma-weighted temperature, or states why it does not
The decision for scoreColor is made deliberately — a near-neutral garment either has a temperature or does not, and the answer is written down
E-034 is resolved and gate 0 stops warning that it carries no guard
features.notes: FILED BY F-031, WHICH FIXED HALF OF IT AND SAID SO. `hueBias` returns 0.867 for a warm grey at OKLCh C = 0.012 — more strongly warm than the corpus’s most saturated red at 0.644 — because a hue angle at that chroma is a rounding artefact of two tiny a and b components. F-031 introduced `temperatureOf`, which scales by chroma against the published lexicon’s 0.039 boundary for "grey", and wired it into `harmony` and `pairingCoherence` where the defect was DEMONSTRATED to produce a wrong answer (versatility ranking a vivid red as the corpus’s most versatile colour). WHAT IS LEFT, and why it was not just changed: `scoreColor`’s temperature fit and `apps/mobile/src/profile/photo.ts#biasFromHue` still call the raw `hueBias`. Changing scoreColor moves EVERY personal-compatibility score in a shipped, tested engine, and it is not obviously wrong there — "this near-neutral garment is warm" may be a defensible thing to tell somebody whose profile leans warm. THAT IS A PRODUCT QUESTION, not a refactor, and writing a guard before answering it would encode the answer in the check. THE APP’S COPY IS E-032’s SUBJECT TOO and is blocked on the same toolchain: it cannot import this package until pnpm install can run. Doing F-099 first would make this a one-line change instead of two.
